conventions.convention: The forward DFT uses ω = exp(−2πi/M); the inverse uses the conjugate root and divides by M. M = 1 is allowed.

Continuous-time inputs have measurable real and imaginary coordinates integrable on compact subintervals; trajectories are locally absolutely continuous and satisfy the state equation outside a Lebesgue-null set. Countable Choice is explicitly assumed for the Lebesgue measure setting.
The LSTM has no peephole connections or projection. Its gates use coordinatewise sigmoid, its candidate uses tanh, and its matrices and biases are shared across time.

DPLR means A = Λ − PQ*, where * is conjugate transpose. B and C are columns and the scalar output is C*x. Bilinear discretization requires I − ΔA/2 invertible; discrete kernel indexing starts at j = 0 with zero initial state x₋₁.
Filter evaluation receives the transformed vector C̃_M = (I − Ā^M)*C. Its operation count excludes forming this vector from C. A direct term Du_t is separate from the state kernel.

LegS retains its time-dependent factor 1/t. Original HiPPO LagT has diagonal −1. The raw LegT matrix first undergoes the specified nonunitary diagonal similarity; its resulting normal part is then unitarily diagonalized.

The filter transform length is the least power of two M ≥ L. At z = −1 the filter uses the finite direct value (Δ/2)C̃_M*B. Diagonal entries λ_j = −2/Δ contribute constants rather than mapped Cauchy poles.

Numerical Cauchy evaluation uses the positive root order exp(2πik/M), repeated poles are permitted, and accuracy is η max(1,A/d). Costs count variable-precision scalar operations and words, with supplied certified approximations and precision/routing certificates; they do not count bits or certificate construction.

Filter complexity treats r as fixed. Its numerical guarantee requires certified block bounds, correction inverse bounds, Cauchy separation and weight bounds, and an exact partition of entries equal or unequal to −2/Δ. The conditioning factor is κ = 64r w²(b+1)²s.

load_bearing.statement: For invertible D ∈ C^(N×N), U,V ∈ C^(N×r), and W = I_r + V*D⁻¹U, D + UV* is invertible if and only if W is invertible. When invertible, (D + UV*)⁻¹ = D⁻¹ − D⁻¹UW⁻¹V*D⁻¹.

For M = 2^q, q ≥ 0, and F_kj = exp(−2πijk/M), F*F = MI and the inverse DFT is M⁻¹F*. The radix-two procedure computes either transform exactly in O(M log(2+M)) complex arithmetic operations and O(M) space. Two polynomials of degree less than n, n ≥ 1, multiply exactly in O(n log(2+n)) operations and O(n) space by radix-two zero-padding to length at least 2n−1.

For the stated finite DPLR data, Δ > 0, 1 ≤ L ≤ M = 2^q, invertible G = I − ΔA/2, C̃_M = (I − Ā^M)*C, and invertible root-grid diagonal resolvents R(z) and corrections W(z) for z ≠ −1, the length-M truncated generating value is H_M(z) = 2/(1+z)[C̃_M*R(z)B − C̃_M*R(z)P W(z)⁻¹Q*R(z)B]. For even M, H_M(−1) = (Δ/2)C̃_M*B. The four scaled resolvent-block families reduce to (r+1)² roots-of-unity Cauchy products, with λ_j = −2/Δ handled by constants.

For n ≥ 1, M = 2^q ≥ 1, a primitive Mth root ω, complex poles μ_j and weights a_j satisfying μ_j ≠ ω^k for every j,k, the balanced product-tree procedure computes y_k = Σ_j a_j/(ω^k−μ_j) exactly using O((n+M) log²(2+n+M)) complex arithmetic operations and O(n+M) space. Repeated poles are allowed.

For n ≥ 0, M = 2^q ≥ 1, z_k = exp(2πik/M), complex weights and poles with |z_k−μ_j| ≥ d > 0, A ≥ Σ_j|a_j|, s = max(1,A/d), and 0 < η ≤ 1/2, approximations satisfy max_k|ŷ_k−y_k| ≤ ηs using O((n+M) log(2+M) log(1/η)) scalar operations and O(n+M) scalar words. This uses the stated certified variable-precision arithmetic, supplied constants, routing enclosures and finite-circuit precision certificate, excluding bit cost and construction of supplied constants/certificates. Absolute error δ, 0 < δ ≤ 1/2, costs O((n+M) log(2+M) log(s/δ)).

For N,r ≥ 1, A = Λ − PQ* with diagonal Λ, B,C ∈ C^N, Δ > 0, and invertible G = I − ΔA/2, one bilinear recurrent update and scalar output cost O(N(r+1)²+(r+1)³) exact complex arithmetic operations and O(N(r+1)+(r+1)²) working space. For fixed r both are O(N). An invertible diagonal base has an invertible Woodbury correction; a singular diagonal base with invertible G has an invertible bordered correction of size at most 2r.

For the stated fixed-rank DPLR model, Δ > 0, invertible bilinear matrix and all required root-grid diagonal resolvents/corrections, M the least power of two ≥ L, and supplied C̃_M = (I−Ā^M)*C, the filter procedure returns K_L using at most (r+1)² Cauchy products, O((N+L) log²(2+N+L)) exact operations and O(N+L) working space. Under the additional certified numerical bounds, exact exceptional-entry partition and variable-precision circuit hypotheses in the Statement, it achieves infinity-norm error ε, 0 < ε ≤ 1/2, in O((N+L) log(2+N+L) log(κ/ε)) scalar operations and O(N+L) scalar words, where κ = 64r w²(b+1)²s. Counts exclude forming C̃_M, certificate construction and bit cost, and imply no complete training-cost or empirical accuracy guarantee.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit Countable Choice assumption in the continuous-time model's Lebesgue measure setting.
Coordinatewise Lebesgue integrability of continuous-time inputs on compact subintervals.
The epsilon–delta definition of absolute continuity used for state trajectories.
The measurable-set family and restricted Lebesgue set function used in the continuous-time definition.
Under Countable Choice, the Lebesgue-measurable sets form a sigma-algebra and Lebesgue measure is complete.
Measurability of bounded intervals with arbitrary endpoint conventions, followed by the continuous-time definition's countable-union argument for general intervals.
Unitary diagonalization of the normal parts of the three explicitly decomposed HiPPO generators.

concerns.concern: The Definition includes the standalone complexity assertion, “This root search and reindexing use $O(M)$ operations.” The assertion is sound and is justified in thm-cauchy-matvec-at-roots-of-unity-exact-cost, Proof 2.2, but the dispatch's algorithm rule places complexity properties in separate proved result items rather than in the defining procedure.

The Definition instructs calling alg-cauchy-matvec-at-roots-of-unity on the root grid, then says, “The root $-1$ is handled directly and is never included in this Cauchy evaluation.” The called algorithm evaluates all M roots and has no excluded-root input. For even M it therefore also evaluates the auxiliary Cauchy sums at −1. Those evaluations are harmless: lem-s4-convolution-root-of-unity-reduction, Proof 1.2, proves that no mapped nonexceptional pole equals −1. The instructions should distinguish discarding that auxiliary output from excluding the root from the called routine.
